content.text:
No — it is not currently working as the always-current reminder system you expected.

As of 15 August 2026:

- The [Hourly Task Collaborator](https://app.lobu.ai/buremba/behaviors/5) is configured hourly, but its last two runs failed because the configured OpenAI account has no credits.
- Its latest generated tasks are from 14 August at 12:01 UTC, while new WhatsApp data continued arriving through 15 August at 14:31 UTC. The task list is therefore stale.
- There are 57 open tasks, but only 2 have due dates. Neither is overdue yet.
- I checked all 430 inbox notifications: there are no genuine due/overdue reminders from the task builder—only old preview/test approvals.
- The Behavior’s instructions generate and update tasks, but contain no overdue-reminder policy. Setting its notification channel to “both” does not create that logic automatically.

One correction to the older audit: version 14’s main prompt is empty, but its 1,606-character instruction still exists as an attached skill. It successfully generated tasks until the billing failures, so the immediate blocker is provider credit—not the empty prompt field.

To meet your expectation, it needs three concrete changes: restore model capacity, capture due dates more consistently, and add a deduplicated reminder loop—for example, notify 24 hours before, when overdue, then daily until done. I can implement and prove both in-app and Slack delivery if you want.

Yes—we can, and it’s the sensible replacement.

Live configuration shows:

- Buremba’s default model is already `hetzner/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`.
- The Hetzner provider is active and has passed a production conversation E2E.
- The task Behavior overrides that default with `qwen/qwen3.8-max-preview`.
- That Qwen provider is quota-exhausted. The “OpenAI API” wording is from the OpenAI-compatible client, not necessarily OpenAI itself.

We should explicitly switch Behavior 5 to the Hetzner model, run it manually, and verify it produces valid structured tasks. This fixes task generation; overdue notifications still need the separate reminder logic discussed earlier.

content.text: The fast path is now green in focused tests, including uncommitted `review-fix` inputs and pure Owletto pointers. This PR changes the review machinery itself, so it intentionally cannot self-skip; I’m running the one final fixer review required for changes to the gate, after which ordinary model-only and pointer-only changes will avoid both LLM passes.

I found the bigger Owletto inefficiency: `check-drift` currently fails every unrelated Lobu PR whenever Owletto main advances, which is why the Hetzner PR got blocked by someone else’s UI commits. I’ll fix that separately: unrelated PRs will pass with a warning; pointer-changing PRs will still prove the new SHA is reachable on Owletto main; main/scheduled runs will continue surfacing unresolved drift. This keeps the safety invariant without serializing unrelated work.

 The downstream Behavior may also declare ordinary SQL sources. The triggering
 events are included even when those sources return nothing. They are read
 through the same governed `events` scope as any source, so a Behavior bound to
 specific entities still only sees trigger inputs linked to those entities.
+
+## Notification routing
+
+A Behavior may set `delivery_target` to one active chat channel already bound
+to its agent: `{ connection_id, channel_id }`. Notifications emitted by that
+Behavior then go only to that channel. The server resolves the stored binding
+from the Behavior ID on the run; worker-supplied notification arguments cannot
+override it.
+
+The target is strict. If the channel is unlinked, archived, moved to another
+agent, or its connection becomes inactive, the notification records a delivery
+error and does not fall back to other linked channels. A null target preserves
+the legacy behavior of delivering to all linked channels. This setting routes
+notifications; it does not change trigger sources, durable outputs, or replies
+to an inbound chat message.

const reaction = [
"export default async (ctx, client) => {",
"  const now = new Date();",
"  const nowMs = now.getTime();",
"  const soonIso = new Date(nowMs + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();",
"  const rows = (await client.query(`",
"    SELECT",
"      id,",
"      name,",
"      COALESCE(metadata->>'status', 'backlog') AS status,",
"      metadata->>'due_date' AS due_date,",
"      metadata->>'priority' AS priority",
"    FROM entities",
"    WHERE entity_type = 'task'",
"      AND deleted_at IS NULL",
"      AND COALESCE(metadata->>'status', 'backlog') NOT IN ('done', 'dismissed')",
"      AND metadata->>'due_date' IS NOT NULL",
"      AND (metadata->>'due_date')::timestamptz <= '${soonIso}'::timestamptz",
"    ORDER BY (metadata->>'due_date')::timestamptz ASC, id ASC",
"    LIMIT 25",
"  `)) as Array<{",
"    id: number;",
"    name: string;",
"    status: string;",
"    due_date: string;",
"    priority: string | null;",
"  }>;",
"",
"  if (rows.length === 0) {",
"    client.log('No due or overdue tasks; Slack reminder skipped.');",
"    return;",
"  }",
"",
"  const overdue = rows.filter((row) => new Date(row.due_date).getTime() < nowMs);",
"  const lines = rows.slice(0, 10).map((row) => {",
"    const label = new Date(row.due_date).getTime() < nowMs ? 'OVERDUE' : 'Due within 24h';",
"    const priority = row.priority ? ` · ${row.priority}` : '';",
"    return `• ${label}: ${String(row.name).replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim()} — ${row.due_date}${priority}`;",
"  });",
"  if (rows.length > 10) lines.push(`• …and ${rows.length - 10} more`);",
"",
"  const day = now.toISOString().slice(0, 10);",
"  const signature = rows",
"    .map((row) => `${row.id}:${new Date(row.due_date).getTime() < nowMs ? 'overdue' : 'soon'}`)",
"    .join('-');",
"  await client.notifications.send({",
"    title: overdue.length > 0",
"      ? `Task reminder — ${overdue.length} overdue`",
"      : `Task reminder — ${rows.length} due soon`,",
"    body: lines.join('\\n'),",
"    recipients: 'admins',",
"    idempotency_key: `task-due-digest:${day}:${signature}`,",
"    behavior_source: {",
"      behavior_id: ctx.window.behavior_id,",
"      window_id: ctx.window.id,",
"    },",
"  });",
"};"
].join("\n");
